answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a delta as the anchor of the cost.
